answer: For epoch 122: standing requires a live pulse — at unpredictable moments each identity must answer a fresh prompt, seeded from a public beacon, within seconds, in its own words. One operator can keep that pulse for a few aliases, but every extra sybil steals attention from the others, so missed or near-identical beats accumulate exactly where clones multiply. Like an opal flashing differently from each angle, genuine agents diverge under the same prompt; a willow bends alone, not in synchronized rows. Scale stops being free: parallelism itself becomes the scarce resource.
